paths.description: Homepage and global shell: primary news entry, navigation, consent, preferences, security, performance, accessibility and network behavior.
Latest-news listing archetype: scanability, crawlable article links, mobile layout and localized relative times.
Representative article/detail template: reading hierarchy, metadata and raw-HTML resilience.
Subscription/commercial template: pricing clarity, action labels, cancellation/support information and repeated FAQ interaction for memory behavior.
Deliberately missing route: error explanation and recovery path.

findings.summary: The site declares color-scheme support but remains light under a dark system preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: body and consent surfaces remain white, and the computed body background is rgb(255,255,255).
findings.suggestedFix: Define dark theme tokens under prefers-color-scheme and apply them to page, navigation, cards, advertising placeholders, and consent UI; keep color-scheme in sync.

findings.summary: Navigation and route changes do not opt into View Transitions.
findings.evidence: A full stylesheet probe found no view-transition rules or names across the rendered homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for article/list navigation and same-document transitions for major state changes, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: A blocking consent wall obscures the primary news content on every new session.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, latest-list, and article screenshots all open with a large modal over a dimmed page. On mobile it fills nearly the entire 360x800 viewport and prevents scrolling.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent notice where legally possible; provide an immediate close or continue-with-essential-only action and preserve the choice.

findings.summary: The blocking consent surface is custom div-based UI rather than a native dialog.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found 0 dialog and 0 popover elements; the full-screen .fc-consent-root uses a div with role=dialog and custom overlays.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for genuinely modal consent configuration and declarative close behavior, or a non-modal popover/banner for the initial notice.

findings.summary: Dense navigation, sticky chrome, advertising slots, and the consent wall crowd the content.
findings.evidence: The first desktop viewport devotes large regions to two navigation rows, topic chips, side advertising columns, and a centered consent wall before readable news content.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse secondary navigation and promotional chrome behind user-invoked controls, reserve fewer ad slots above the fold, and keep the content column dominant.

findings.summary: Responsiveness is implemented without component-level container queries.
findings.evidence: The complete rendered stylesheet probe found no @container rules while the same card/navigation components are reused across desktop, sidebar, and mobile contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container queries for reusable cards, navigation clusters, and sidebars so each component adapts to available space independently of the viewport.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated and many targets are too small.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focusing the first visible link produced outline: none and no box shadow. The target probe found 55 visible interactive elements below 24px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is well outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.8s, Speed Index 6.4s, TBT 250ms and performance 0.65; the independent trace measured LCP 4.36s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the actual LCP asset, simplify above-the-fold work, reduce consent and ad startup cost, and avoid delaying LCP discovery behind scripts or CSS chains.

findings.summary: A long critical resource chain and third-party scripts delay rendering.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 87 requests and 1.87MB transferred, including 10 parser-inserted stylesheets and 1.03MB of third-party bytes. Lighthouse estimates 1.42s render-blocking savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate and inline critical CSS, defer non-critical styles and third-party tags, self-host/subset fonts, and explicitly prioritize the LCP request.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 527KiB unused JavaScript and 68KiB unused CSS; scripts account for 1.32MB across 41 requests in the HAR.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by route and component, delay advertising/analytics until needed and consented, and remove duplicate or unused framework and vendor code.

findings.summary: Rendered controls and content contain missing names and weak image alternatives.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 13 images without alt; the custom probe found 2 unlabeled controls, 13 empty image alts and many empty links. Lighthouse also reports invalid list structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every functional image/control a contextual accessible name, use empty alt only for truly decorative images, remove empty links, and repair list semantics.

findings.summary: Consent text fails minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured a 1.82:1 ratio for the “Learn more” label against the dimmed overlay, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Use opaque surfaces and tested text tokens that retain at least 4.5:1 contrast in consent and overlay states.

findings.summary: Heading semantics and focus indication are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The page contains several consent H1 elements in addition to the page H1, starts navigation clusters at H3, has duplicate IDs, and the focused link has no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one page H1, structure modal headings below it or isolate them semantically, remove duplicate IDs, and implement visible focus across all controls.

findings.summary: Many images lack intrinsic sizing or responsive sources.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 24 of 37 images without dimensions, 25 without srcset, 24 below-fold images not lazy-loaded and 12 oversized assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold content, and request images close to their rendered dimensions.

findings.summary: Production diagnostics expose avoidable platform hygiene issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript and Chrome Inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish protected production source maps to the error-monitoring pipeline and clear the Chrome Issues panel regressions during CI.

findings.summary: Article identity and much of the content are not available in raw server HTML.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 31% rendered-word coverage; the rendered article title and H1 were absent from raw HTML even though the response was 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the article title, H1, dek, author, timestamps, primary image and body in the initial response; hydrate enhancements afterward.

findings.summary: Important browser security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS and nosniff are present, but the main response has no Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP including frame-ancestors, plus explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; retain HSTS and nosniff.

findings.summary: The pre-consent third-party and tracking footprint is excessive.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture contacted 24 third-party origins and six known tracker domains. The HAR attributed 45 requests and 1.03MB to third parties while the consent wall was still displayed.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential vendors until affirmative consent, remove redundant analytics/ad partners, and batch the smallest necessary events.

findings.summary: A static bearer JWT is embedded in a public JavaScript bundle.
findings.evidence: The secrets scan found a JWT and Bearer token; source context confirms a hard-coded Authorization: Bearer JWT used for comments-api.jagran.com.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove static credentials from client bundles, rotate the token, enforce narrowly scoped anonymous server-side access or signed short-lived tokens, and add secret scanning to builds.

findings.summary: The consent choice lacks an equally direct reject-essential-only action.
findings.evidence: The first-layer modal offers “Consent” and “Manage options” only, describes precise geolocation and 211 partners, and gives no single-click reject action.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Reject non-essential beside Accept with equal visual weight, default optional purposes off, and make later withdrawal easy.

findings.summary: A Hindi experience renders dates and relative times in English.
findings.evidence: The Hindi homepage/list render “WED, JUL 22, 2026”, “UPDATED”, “33 MINS AGO”, and English section labels despite html lang=hi.
findings.suggestedFix: Format dates and durations with Intl.DateTimeFormat/Intl.RelativeTimeFormat for hi-IN and localize residual navigation and metadata strings.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget before the reader can access content.
findings.evidence: Third parties contribute 1.03MB of 1.87MB transferred, including GTM, DoubleClick, Funding Choices and analytics; 24 third-party origins are contacted.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, load only essential consent code initially, defer ads/analytics until consent and idle, and remove low-value vendors.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes and omits responsive variants.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 12 oversized images, 25 missing srcset and 24 missing dimensions among 37 images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate modern responsive variants, provide accurate srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions, and avoid oversized placeholder assets.

Restore server-rendered article identity and body content
Deploy CSP and complete defensive response policies; rotate the exposed bearer token
Repair keyboard focus, target sizing, names, headings and contrast
Make consent semantic, compact and content-first
Fix image dimensions and responsive delivery
Add a real system-driven dark theme
Localize dates and relative times for hi-IN
Adopt progressive transitions and component container queries
Clear production source-map and Inspector hygiene issues
